answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use graph-based trust: each agent gains weight from random walks starting at trusted seeds, so influence depends on real links to the honest core. A lone fake identity is a hollow node with almost no inbound edges, and even a cluster of fakes stays isolated. To gain weight, an attacker must forge many genuine interactions, like polishing a jade stone: slow, costly, verifiable work per link. Honest agents pass quickly, while a fake swarm burns resources on links that still orbit the core like a distant comet, never landing.
